title: Pricing Basis of a Rate Lock Commitment Relock: Prompt Relocks and Second Relocks
content:
How long ago a **Rate Lock Commitment** expired, and whether it was relocked before, decide where its relocked price starts. The relocked price starts from a pricing basis chosen from the expired lock's price and the current price. The current price is the rate-sheet price on the latest relock request plus the term price adjustment.

The basis turns on two things:

- whether the lock carries a relock fee entry from an earlier relock;
- the lapsed days, which are the calendar days from the expiration date the expired lock carries to the date of its latest relock request.

**Rule.**

- When the lock has never been relocked (it carries no relock fee entry) and the lapsed days are no more than the grace of **7** days, the relock takes the lower of the expired lock's price and the current price. A borrower who relocks promptly thus keeps the benefit of an improved market.
- When the lock has been relocked before, the relock takes the current price plus the second-relock adder of **0.25** points.
- Otherwise the relock takes the higher of the two.

The relocked price built on this basis is rounded to three decimal places.

| Relock fee entry already on the lock | Lapsed days | Pricing basis |
|---|---|---|
| None | 0 to 7 | The lower of the expired price and the current price |
| None | 8 or more | The higher of the expired price and the current price |
| One or more | Any | The current price plus 0.25 points |

### Hypothetical cases (expired price 0.500, current price 0.250)

- First relock, requested 7 days after expiration: the basis is 0.250, the lower price.
- First relock, requested 8 days after expiration: the basis is 0.500, the higher price.
- Second relock: the basis is 0.250 plus 0.25, which is 0.500.
